Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Hi all,

Attached are the technical artifacts for the Medicore packet. Key points below (short summary for procurement):

- VPC topology: Private Deploy (customer VPC peering) to a dedicated EU tenant pool. No public NAT egress from the serving instances unless explicitly configured by the customer. VPC peering uses private IPs and route tables are restricted to the peered prefixes. (See vpc-architecture-diagram.pdf)

- Egress controls & logging: All outbound flows from the tenant pool are routed through a managed egress gateway located in the chosen EU region; we apply egress allow-lists and require approval for cross-border peers. Flow logs and connection metadata are retained for 90 days by default and can be adjusted per contract. (See egress-flow-trace.png)

- KMS & key residency: Customers may bring a customer-managed key (CMK) via supported KMS providers in-region. By default, Redwood-managed KMS keys for hosted accounts can be restricted to EU key partitions. Our CAIQ mapping highlights the controls around key management and access reviews. (See caiq-mapping-entries.xlsx)

- SOC 2 / backups: Backups for private deployments are stored in the same EU region by default. We'll attach a short SOC 2 scope note flagging which backups and log archives are within EU.

Files attached to this message: vpc-architecture-diagram.pdf (diagram), caiq-mapping-entries.xlsx (control mapping extract), egress-flow-trace.png (simplified traffic flow).

If Medicore's procurement needs a signed letter, we can prepare a one-page declaration and run it through legal. Stephanie — can you confirm we can sign a regional-scope declaration for this pilot (standard template)?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
